Chapter 1: Growing Up in a World of Hurt and Fear
Imagine starting life in a place where safety is more of a wish than a reality. For a child growing up in the backstreets of Puerto Rico, every day could feel like a test—one where the world never seems quite safe enough. In a small, crowded house, a young boy quickly figured out that love and pain can sometimes be tangled together in ways that are tough to understand.
His parents? They were both carrying heavy burdens of their own. Anger and superstition seemed to fill every corner of their home. His mom, haunted by memories she never shared, sometimes lashed out—leaving wounds no one else could see. And his dad, distracted and distant, just didn’t seem able to offer the comfort every kid hopes for.
Nights were filled with shouting. Days drifted by with a nagging feeling that he just wasn’t wanted.
So, what happens to a young heart in that kind of world? Well, it hardens. He learned to keep his feelings locked away, to expect disappointment, and to think of violence as just... normal life. The streets outside his door didn’t offer much relief, either. Other kids, just as lost and wounded, formed their own tough little groups. Fights would break out over the smallest things. Trust? Rare. Betrayal? Almost expected. Longing for a place to fit in, the boy found himself drawn to the toughest kids—the ones everyone else seemed to fear and respect.
School was no escape. Teachers, overwhelmed by crowded classrooms and endless problems, rarely saw the pain hiding behind his tough guy act. His anger kept bubbling up, making it nearly impossible to focus on lessons or even care about them. Before long, he was branded a troublemaker—someone better avoided or punished. Each failure, every harsh word, just deepened his loneliness.
Back at home, things only got harder. His mom’s superstitions took over—she started turning to spiritualists and odd rituals, desperate to chase away what she called “bad luck.” The boy watched, scared and confused, as strange ceremonies played out right there in their living room. Sometimes, he was the target—told that evil spirits were causing his behavior. Instead of feeling comforted, he felt ashamed... and even more afraid.
As the years rolled by, his heart seemed to turn to ice. He stopped hoping for kindness. All that mattered now was being strong—because in his world, that’s what kept you safe. The streets became his real classroom. He learned how to fight, how to intimidate, and how to never let anyone see what he truly felt inside. The sting of rejection at home was replaced by the rush of being feared out on the street.
Still, under all that toughness, something softer lingered. In those rare, quiet moments, he found himself wondering—could life ever be different? He’d catch glimpses of families laughing together, of kids who actually seemed safe and loved. But those moments felt a million miles away, like dreams that vanish as soon as you wake up.
For now, surviving meant shutting down hope and embracing the only world he knew—a place where love felt like a weakness, and violence was the only language anyone seemed to understand.
